text:
anya (account_exec): Kicking off Skyline POC — they flagged a custom tokenizer that splits product codes oddly, causing embedding drift. Need catalog fit + compatibility check before we send pricing. Any SE available? :wave:

matt (sales_engineer): I can take it. Which model variants are they targeting? They mentioned very long contexts and custom tokenization in their SOW.

anya (account_exec): They asked for ‘open-llm-13k’ variant and a custom tokenization pipeline. Also want Dedicated latency SLO and a pricing ballpark for heavy embed usage.

matt (sales_engineer): Two technical risks: tokenizer -> embedding mismatch, and potential KV-cache misalignment if their tokenization differs at runtime. Can we run a tokenization comparison on a sample? @ingest-bot can you stage their sample file?

ingest-bot: queued sample 'skyline_sample_v1.txt' -> run id 8791. Quick summary: tokenizer_mismatch_rate=0.14, avg_seq_len=1200, sample_count=200. Full diff uploaded to /tmp/8791_diff.log

matt (sales_engineer): 14% mismatch is non-trivial for retrieval/embeddings. We should do an embed-regression test. Also: quantization question — can we serve a quantized 4-bit/8-bit variant without degrading their embedding space?

leo (platform): Short answer: 8-bit can change embedding geometry noticeably. We recommend fp16 or calibrated 4-bit for embeddings with per-token quant calibration. We can run a quick A/B: fp16 vs 4-bit quant on a 50-prompt test set.

anya (account_exec): I'll ask Skyline for 50 representative prompts + 200 doc snippets. Also they started a security questionnaire asking about KMS and logs retention — @jo (legal) any special asks?

jo (legal): For Private deployments they require customer-managed KMS (BYOK) — doable but adds contract clause. For Hosted we can offer BYOK with addendum. Also clarify logs retention window; they want 6 months of audit logs for the POC. I'll draft responses and the ATO checklist (2–3 business days).

matt (sales_engineer): For pricing: if embeddings must run on fp16 (no quant), cost goes up. Rough heuristic: fp16 -> ~2.4x token cost vs heavily-quantized variant. If they require Dedicated capacity + lower latency we can offer reserved pricing. Need a finance sanity check.

finance-team: Quick back-of-envelope: assume 100k embed tokens/day -> ~3M tokens/month. Base hosted (quantized) = ~$0.0008 per 1k -> ~$2.4k/mo. fp16 premium -> ~$0.0019 per 1k -> ~$5.7k/mo. Dedicated reserved (monthly commit) could be ~$4.2k/mo depending on node sizing. These are ballparks — will formalize in quote.

matt (sales_engineer): Next steps I propose:
1) Skyline provides 50 prompts + 200 docs (requested by EOD Tue).
2) SE runs tokenization pass + embed regression; we’ll report mismatch rate and per-prompt embedding cosine diffs.
3) Platform runs fp16 vs 4-bit quant comparison on the prompt set.
4) Legal returns questionnaire answers / KMS path.
5) Finance prepares POC quote for hosted vs dedicated.

matt (sales_engineer): Ops ticket created: https://redwood.ops/tickets/RED-4521 — includes test harness and the token-compare script: ```python
# token compare harness (excerpt)
from redwood.tokenizer import Tokenizer
from redwood.embeddings import EmbeddingClient

base_tok = Tokenizer('catalog/open-llm-13k')
custom_tok = Tokenizer('vendor/skyline-tokenizer-v1')
# run sample diffs...
```

anya (account_exec): Great — Skyline wants to start next Monday, so let's treat this as high priority. I'll ping them for the prompt set now. :rocket:

leo (platform): FYI if SE wants, I can spin a small fp16 test node for the A/B to keep results reproducible. Say when.

matt (sales_engineer): Please spin it. I'll post results in this thread once the regression run finishes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
